utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody this morning. Mr. Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Today the session will take place pursuant to Rule 15 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Judge Harhoff is sitting in Milosevic because they have another witness to lead in that case. Now, I can't say how long he will be away for. It will be for as long as the hearing takes place. Okay. Could we have appearances, please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, Counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis and Matthias Neuner, assisted by our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, our learned friends and everybody in the courtroom and around the courtroom. Vasvija Vidovic and Nicholas Robson representing the Defence of General Delic, assisted by Lejla Gluhic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I believe we don't have the witness in court because something is to be raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I -- I rise to my feet in -- out of an abundance of caution. As I was going home last evening, I believe I observed the current witness, Mr. Hasanagic, standing in front of the Peace Palace with Sead Delic, the previous witness. I made some inquiries with VWS this morning, and Sead Delic is, as we speak, being taken to the airport. So in fact he was here last evening. I don't know for certain that I saw the two of them, but I want to put that on the record so that if the Chamber wishes to ask Mr. Hasanagic if he was, in fact, speaking to Mr. Delic last evening or if the Defence would like to raise that issue with the witness, they may do so. But I simply wanted to put that on the record, that I did observe what I believe to be the two of them standing in front of the Peace Palace about 7.00 or a little bit after last evening. And so I just wanted to raise that issue out of an abundance of caution in the event anyone were to suggest that the two witnesses were doing anything improper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me just understand one little point you've made. You say Mr. Sead Delic is on the way to the airport as we speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes. I -- after I observed -- or what I thought was the two of them last evening, first thing this morning I called victims and Witness section to question them as to when Mr. Delic actually was leaving or had left in the event that I was mistaken. Perhaps he left yesterday. So I made the inquiries with VWS, and they informed me that he was in fact here last night and this morning is -- is being taken to the airport for a flight about 10.30 or 11.00 this morning back to Sarajevo. So it is possible that the two individuals that I observed last evening were in fact Mr. Delic and Mr. Hasanagic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I simply want to put that on the record out of an abundance of caution in the event anyone wishes to question the witness about that. But it did appear to be the two of them. And as I said, Mr. Delic in fact was here last evening. So that -- that might go to the issue of whether the two of them were actually speaking last night. Obviously I don't know about what. I didn't stop and speak to them. I simply continued on my way home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. I waited for the interpretation to finish. What I imagined how the witness and -- Witnesses Service would be doing is not to put witnesses in the same hotel. This is how I imagined how they did about -- went about it. I would like future witnesses to be warned against discussing this case with anybody, witnesses or others, so that we can avoid such situations in the future. And we will see how the evidence develops, what I'm going to decide to ask him about in my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Just to say -- I -- I appreciate what you said, but I just wonder how careful we can be with this kind of -- these people live in Bosnia-Herzegovina, you know. We -- we don't know what they do when they are together there and -- but I take the point from -- we'll do the best we can from our side and we'll warn the witnesses. Okay? Thank you so much. Okay. Let's -- thank you very much, Mr. Mundis. Would you like to call the witness now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hasanagic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Just to remind you that yesterday at the beginning of your testimony you've made a declaration to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but truth. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are still bound by that declaration to tell the truth even today. Okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: At the beginning, I want to clarify that, as my learned colleague has pointed out, Exhibit 447 and 452 are indeed identical, and I here wish to clarify that Exhibit 447 should be omitted because 452 is the same. And I remember the situation as well, and I believe there was a misunderstanding at the time, and I just wish to show the document now, which I wanted to show earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I interrupt? According to -- oh, okay. You are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I was looking at the wrong date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If, please, Exhibit P2236 could be shown. Sorry, I don't get the image. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Ah.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could please move to the signature first, which is on the second page of the B/C/S. No, it's the third page -- no, it's the second on mine. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Whose signature is this?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And do you recognise the document? If you could go back to the first page, please.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is an order for engineering support you're issuing here on the 15th of July, 1995. Could you just explain to the Judges why engineering support is needed.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Engineering support is necessary to secure movement through the deployment of the troops manning the front line, then to overcome enemy obstacles. Then it is necessary to ensure supply of materiel and evacuation of the wounded, to secure the facilities at those lines that were captured, that were reached; in a word, to secure and provide for movement and manoeuvre of those units going on the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With this explanation being given, may I ask that the document be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You said it's already admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: There was a problem. I wanted to show this document yesterday, and instead another document, which turned out to be a duplicate was being shown. And I'm showing this -- after I withdraw the previous document, I'm showing this document now in order to have the right exhibit being admitted into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. That -- okay, I understand that. Just one other point. Now, this document is dated the 15th of July. According to my notes, Exhibit 447, which was PT2236, was dated the 28th of July. So also was PT2337, Exhibit 452. Those were dated the same. On -- I beg your pardon. I understand what you are saying. Thank you so much. I'm too slow on the uptake.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I've got it clear. Okay. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number. Will it be given the same exhibit number as 447.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this will be Exhibit number 447, and the previous 65 ter document, which was P02336, has been withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I want to turn back to the video which we saw about the training yesterday. I'm referring to Exhibit 441.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Hasanagic, the video will not be shown now, but I want to show you a still from this video because you recognised certain persons on the video and we have produced a still overnight. If this could be -- please be placed on the ELMO so that the Defence and the Judges can also see it. Thank you. Could you, first of all, state whom you're seeing here, if you recognise anybody.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this photo, this is me; this is Ajman, the interpreter; the Fehim Skulj, commander of the 329th Brigade; and I don't know this person. I'm not sure I saw him on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... You don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Which person you don't recognise, please? You said one person you don't recognise.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And you say he's the -- he's the what of the 329th?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you for the Judge please clarify who is the person from the 329th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one, this person.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you above his head mark a "1", please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Find out his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you mark above this person's head a "1" and state clearly for the record his name.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the commander of the 329th Brigade, Fehim Skulj.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And could you mark above the person's head whom you believe to be Ajman, number "2".

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. This is the interpreter, Ajman.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And could you mark above your own head a number "3", please.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you mark a question mark above the person's head whom you don't know.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can this please be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The photograph is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 454.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to change the topic now. We talked yesterday about Proljece II. And what I'm interested in is I want to talk about prisoners of war. We talked next to Proljece II about other combat operations, Manevar, Sabur, Proljece, Proljece II. Could you clarify for the Judges, during Operation Manevar, were there any POWs taken by the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During Manevar 94, there were no POWs. No prisoners were taken during Sabur, only then.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So no prisoners of war taken during Manevar 94 and Sabur. Were there prisoners of war taken during Proljece operation, which was in May 1995?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were no POWs in Proljece 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: How was it during Proljece II, which was in July 1995, as you explained to us, were there POWs taken?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: How many, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the number, but I know that there were some prisoners taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you know which unit took the POWs?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The unit that was there, the El Mujahedin Detachment, together with other units that worked in coordinated action.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And do you recall which other units who coordinated with them the action were involved in the taking of POWs?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other units did not take prisoners, but 328th Brigade was deployed in the area of where the El Mujahedin Detachment passed through.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. So to clarify, the only unit who took POWs, then, was which unit?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that occasion, the El Mujahedin Detachment took prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And do you know the fate of these prisoners?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ultimately I heard that they were exchanged, all of them, and that they are all safe and sound.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to show you document PT2278. You see here on the first page it's from the 27th of July, 1995. And if we could go for the second -- only in the B/C/S to the last page to see the signature. Could you please state who signed this document.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I signed this. This is a regular report to the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm interested in the third page of the B/C/S and the seventh page of the English translation which corresponds. If you look under the heading number 6, "Security situation," could you tell us who is providing information relating to security situation in your report.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This information has been prepared by the security organ, and it is regulated in the order what the treatment of the POWs is to be. And on the basis of that, he wrote this item in the report, as is stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who wrote -- who wrote this item? Who is the security organ you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is a -- the security organ is an integral part of the division command, and they prepared this item in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And do you know who prepared it? If not, I can move on.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, this was prepared by the security organ within its purview.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. In your report, it states here that war prisoners and documents have been captured from the aggressor formations and that these are not forwarded according to the instructions. Could you just explain to the Judges which documents are envisaged or are meant here.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are documents captured in the area of disposition of the enemy forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And which enemy forces? Which army are you referring to here by "enemy forces"?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Army of the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And it says that they are not forwarded. What does that mean? What value have documents who need to be forwarded?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the captured documents contain certain information that may help us to continue with our combat activities, to know about the composition of the enemy forces and everything else that may be contained therein, what are the enemy's ideas, proposals for going forward. These were very important documents for our continued activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what is the value of war prisoners?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same. It would be possible to find out certain things from them in the area that they occupied.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You are informing with your document here the 3rd Corps. Did you get any response from the 3rd Corps in relation to the forwarding of war -- or the non-forwarding of war prisoners and captured documents?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember whether I received any response.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: For clarification, which war -- which unit took the war prisoners and the captured documents here?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said a while ago members of the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can the document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 455.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to move to the next document, PT2284. The previous document was from the 21st of July at 18.30 hours, and we will see the date on this document. It is, as we can see, the next day in the evening, 9.30. If we could please look for a second in the B/C/S only at the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who wrote this signature?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did. That's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if we could go back to page 1, please. And I'm interested in roughly line 8 from the bottom. In the English version, it is page 2, the last paragraph. To help you find the paragraph, I start in English after -- the sentence starts in English: "After interrogating the imprisoned Chetniks and checking their personal documents, it was established that most of the imprisoned Chetniks were from Prnjavor, and that some among them were of Muslim faith." Do you find this?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You're reporting here about imprisoned Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What group are you referring to here? Who are the imprisoned Chetniks?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were soldiers of the Army of the Republika Srpska who were captured during these combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So are you referring to the same or to a different group? I'm talking about the previous document now. Are we talking about the same group?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same group.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The group you're reporting about on the 21st of July in the evening already, yeah?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who interrogated them?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were supposed to be interrogated at the battalion command first. That's the first command post. And then the brigade command and the division command. I can't tell you who in fact interrogated them, but this was supposed to be the order in which they were supposed to be interrogated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you know who provided you with this information which you put in your report?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This information was provided by the security and intelligence organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And would you know a name of the security or a name of this intelligence organ?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The head of the security organ was Fadil Imamovic, and the head of the -- the intelligence organ is Izudin Hajdarhodzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you clarify the name of the security organ, because the interpreters didn't catch it fully.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Izudin Hajdarhodzic was the head of the intelligence organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And they both provided this information?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They wrote it combat activities continued on the 21st and the 22nd. They wrote the information under the heading which was their duty to write within the report and then I signed it. I don't remember this specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can the document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 456.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to move to PT2306. I apologise, 2301, PT2301. Could you just look at the signature, please. Who wrote the signature?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if we could scroll up in the -- in the B/C/S. I see here in the upper right-hand corner - if we can scroll up, please - "Proljece 95-3." Could you explain what that stands for.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Proljece II was conducted on the 21st and the 22nd. After we achieved -- or after we were successful, the corps commander received a proposal to let some other units of the corps be involved in the continuation of the action. He redeployed elements of the forces in the area of responsibility of the division to exploit the successes achieved; however, they did not manage to advance any further. The enemy consolidated his forces and pushed us back to the positions we held on the 21st, which meant that we had lost all that we managed to achieve on the 21st and the 22nd.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could the document please be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is this document telling us? Can we just see what it tells us before ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document says that the corps commander decided to redeploy the forces it had on the Sarajevo theatre of war into the area of responsibility of the division in order to exploit the successes achieved. He was together with me at the command post.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 457.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Since you just mentioned the corps commander, can Exhibit PT2306 please be shown. You see, it's a document from the 23rd of July, 1995. And if we could go to your signature only in the B/C/S version, please -- sorry, if we could go to the signature. I want to find out who signed it.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm interested in the second page of the B/C/S; namely, the third hyphen above section number 3. And in English, it's page 3, the second paragraph. It starts with "During the day, the 3rd Corps commander and General Karisik." Do you find it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. The English is displayed. Can we scroll the English up, please. Yes. It's the second paragraph here. It's the third hyphen above the headline number 3.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you explain --

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you explain what happens here?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've just told you that when these forces arrived, the corps commander arrived with them. Ultimately, I had all the attacking forces in my area of responsibility, including the corps commander, who was there and who took the command over, so he was in command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you say from which level of the army General Karisik is?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he was from the General Staff of the BH army, but believe me when I tell you that I don't know which position he held.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: How long did the two gentlemen stay at Klek command post?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the corps commander stayed there longer, but I wouldn't be able to tell you how long. The combat activities were ongoing and all my attentions were focused on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: How long did General Karisik stay?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've just told you that I wouldn't be able to say; for the same reason, that I was focused on the combat activities. I just met up with them. We discussed the situation, and I went back to the attacking forces to direct them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can the document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 458.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm interested in PT2312. Can this please be shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We just saw it's a document from the 24th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could only in the B/C/S please the signature on the last page be -- be shown.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who signed this?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could the English be centralised so that we can read, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to have the fourth page in the -- of the English please be displayed. The last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I didn't see whether this was a report or a piece of information, a brief. Can we have page 1, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can we have the first page for the witness shown, please, in B/C/S. The English can stay as it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, we'd like also to see what it is all about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's a brief on the combat activities in the area of the 35th Division. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we now move to -- B/C/S to the second page; and English, to the fourth page. And in B/C/S, which is being displayed now, I'm interested in the third paragraph above section 2. And in English, it is the fourth page, the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It starts, for you, Mr. Hasanagic, with [B/C/S spoken]. Do you find this line?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. It says here, if I quote correctly: "Eleven members of the work platoons of Muslim nationality were captured as well as 12 Chetniks." Do you find that?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What I'm interested in, about which group of prisoners are we talking about? This is a --

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a brief for the corps commander. Since Proljece II, on the 21st and 22nd and 23rd, when it was ongoing, the corps commander was present in the Sarajevo theatre of war. Later on I was requested to provide information about what had happened. Among other things, we wrote that 11 members of work platoons, detailed platoons, were captured. These were Muslims who were part of the Prnjavor Brigade. They were brought over from Prnjavor to dig trenches, to make fortifications along their lines, and to be at their service. This time we also have the number of soldiers of the VRS who were captured, as well as the assets that were captured in that action.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And who captured these soldiers, the 12 Chetniks? Which unit?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already said, the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: For clarification, you are reporting for the third time about the same group of captured.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can the document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Before we do that, can I just -- sorry. Before we do that, can I just get clarity. Witness, you're saying that those 12 Chetniks belonged to which -- to the VRS, isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And the 11 members of work platoons who were of Muslim origin were to what army did they belong?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were forcibly conscripted by the Army of the Republika Srpska. They were forcibly mobilised and were taken from Prnjavor to Ozren in order to dig trenches and to carry out any other activities they were ordered to carry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 459.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to show you document PT2356. You can see here it's a document from the 2nd of August, 1995. And I want, only for the B/C/S version on the screen that the signature on the last page is being shown. And who signed the signature is my question. Or who made the signature?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my signature. I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And the handwriting?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wrote: "Take measures against commanding officers" -- or rather, "senior officers and commanders." I don't recall what this was about. In other words, I ordered that measures be taken to -- against senior officers and commands -- or actually, it doesn't say "commanders" but "ring leaders."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. I want to draw your attention to page 2 of the B/C/S, which is page 4 in the English version, the last paragraph of the English version there. And I'm interested in section 3(c) of your document.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "Factories positively impacting on combat morale. The commander of the 35th Division, President of the Presidency, Izetbegovic, the commander of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Rasim Delic; and the commander of the 3rd Corps, Sakib Mahmuljin."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It says here that they visited the command of the 35th Division. Could you explain what happened during this visit.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First the visit took place at the local municipal authorities of Zavidovici, and I was there and together with the representatives of the Zavidovici municipality, I received the commanders. I spent a short period of time there and went back to the division command. I reported to the President. We entered one of the offices where we sat at a table. I presented the situation in the division to the commanders there briefly. The army commander was making notes. I don't know how long the meeting lasted. Maybe some 30 to 40 minutes. I can't be more specific than that. Soon thereafter I went out of the office, leaving them in the office -- leaving them behind in the office on their own.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what happened then?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my duty officers, I found out later on, as I spoke to them in one of the corridors, that some Mujahedin had passed through there. What sort of conversations took place, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. First I want to clarify. You said you left them in the office. Who -- who was left behind when you left the office?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: President Izetbegovic and the commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Which commanders? Please name them.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The republic's army commander, Rasim Delic; and Sakib Mahmuljin.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And they were in which office?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the offices next to mine. I can't recall exactly which one it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And then you said that your duty officers told you that some Mujahedin had passed through there. Can you explain what you mean by "some Mujahedin."

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know how it is. The soldiers who were around just said to me, "Some Mujahedin passed by." They didn't know anything else, and I didn't inquire any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And "some Mujahedin," are you referring to a unit here by saying "some Mujahedin"? Could you just clarify.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since I went there to prepare the division command for reporting, I presumed them to have been members of the Mujahedin detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you stated they -- your soldiers or duty officers told you they passed by. What do you mean or what did they mean at the time by "passing by"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. I find this quite interesting. How should the witness know what these persons thought as they were saying these things? This is calling for speculation, quite a -- obviously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'll rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What did you mean when you stated a moment ago "they passed by"?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what to tell you. Quite simply, that they went past. They passed by. I don't know what you want me to say. I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did -- did you get any indication of the movement from your duty officer, of the movement of the -- sorry, I'll rephrase. Did you get any indication of the movement of the El Mujahedin Detachment members by your duty officers? In which direction they moved?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. There was a corridor there and the -- from the corridor -- along the corridor you had the offices there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And where were the Mujahedin -- El Mujahedin Detachment members seen in relation to the corridor?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you. They were seen in the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you yourself see anybody?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I saw Ajman there, but that was before the President and the commanders arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And where did you see Ajman?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of the division command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And the meeting we are -- okay. How many -- how much time before the President and Delic and -- Rasim Delic and Mahmuljin approved? How much time before did you see Ajman at the command post of the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived there from the municipality to prepare the command for the report to the President and commander, I can't specify the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you see Rasim Delic later that day again?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't go out in the field after that, so as a host I sent them on their way.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you saw him again. Did Mr. Delic mention anything to you?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did Mr. -- did you see Mr. Izetbegovic and Mr. Mahmuljin that day again?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They departed from the division command together.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Together with whom?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The President and the commanders went with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You say "with him." Who was "him"?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: President Izetbegovic was the most senior person, and they accompanied him. It's only logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So Mr. Mahmuljin, Mr. Delic, and Mr. Izetbegovic departed together. And in which direction; do you know? Where were they going to?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to have the document tendered into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 460.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to move to a completely different topic, operation -- the September operation, September 1995 operation. I wish to show document PT2452 to you. Have you ever seen this document?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. If you could go to the second page of the B/C/S, please, to look at the date, which is the 25th of August, 1995. And move to the third-last page in the B/C/S for a moment to look at the signature. Who signed?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I signed this. This is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you, if we move back to the first page for a moment, explain what this document is about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I thought the witness says he's never seen this document, even though he claims he signed it. Are you able to explain the contents of this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What do you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never saw the front page, the cover page that was shown a minute ago. Not this one but the one that says "Order."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. Then I confine myself to this page. The second page now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you explain, first of all, what in the upper right --

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 5-8 -- I apologise. Let us go to the front or the cover page, please. This first page has not been signed by corps commander. I don't think this is my original order. This order was produced on several occasions. The original order is signed by the corps commander and by me and it bears stamps on each page, and that is the original order. Why was it produced on several occasions? Because the documents that kept coming and going had to be amended and a document is valid only when it is signed by the corps commander or when he approves that document. I -- there is no such approval on this page, and I'm not sure whether the contents are the right contents, because there is no rubber stamp on each page. This was done precisely for the reason that there were several copies or variations of this order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So do I understand you to be talking about this page that you say you had never seen? Because the rest of the document you signed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you explain what "F-95" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: He doesn't know this one. Go to the pages that he knows. He says this first page he doesn't know. He doesn't -- doesn't got a stamp -- it hasn't got his signature. It hasn't got the 3rd Corps stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. We are going --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is the contents of the document that is ...

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I take Your Honour's suggestion on board. Could we go to page 2, please, in B/C/S and English.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you explain what on the upper right-hand side "F-95" stands for?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name of the September operation is Farz 95, and this is the abbreviated version, "F-95."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Farz 95 or F-95 relates to which operation?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Vozuca operation, in September.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. You said earlier at some point in time Sakib Mahmuljin signed the first page. Could you explain a little bit the process leading to Sakib Mahmuljin finally signing the first page.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The idea for the liberation of Vozuca was long in coming. As I said, we had undertaken some actions to get as close to Vozuca as possible. The key objective of the Vozuca operation was the Paljenik feature. We had attempted to resolve that matter on four or five occasions previously, and at one of the meetings at corps command we discussed how should we go about resolving the issue of the Vozuca and how we should go about resolving the issue of the Ribnica-Zavidovici road. The commander came up with this idea and said that all corps units are going to take part in this operation. That operation was in the area of responsibility of the 35th Division, and that this operation would be undertaken in corporation with the 2nd Corps. And that was the start of the planning and preparation process for this operation; meaning the preparation of documents, the preparation of facilities, roads for supply and evacuation, training, and everything that is understood by the term "preparation." Until the combat operations, this is a process. It is not a static thing. It doesn't take one day. All commanders received the basic idea of the corps commander underpinning this operation. At subsequent meetings, we elaborated about how we should resolve all the outstanding issues, that we agreed all subordinated commanders together with the corps commander, we agreed that Podsijelovo facility or Podsijelovo feature was the key to the operation. And the commander on that occasion said to all of us that the El Mujahedin Detachment is going to attack the Paljenik feature to try to resolve the matter of the Paljenik feature, given what had been going on around that feature in -- previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I interrupt you. You said a moment ago "the commander said on that occasion." To which commander? Can you name the commander? To which commander are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corps commander, Sakib Mahmuljin.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you're referring obviously to meetings. Could you say how many times you met the corps commander or his staff until you finally put the signature below the document in front of you.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's difficult to remember on how many occasions. Maybe two or three times with the commander, then two or three times with his staff, his assistants, branch commanders, logistics. On several occasions. Because this was a significant operation and that operation was planned and controlled and managed by the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Before the break, can I have -- can I tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 461.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Is that a convenient time? Thank you very much. We'll take a break and come back at quarter to 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we could please go for one second back to Exhibit 461, which was shown before the break, and to the second-last page in the B/C/S only. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you just explain -- it's unfortunately divided into two pieces. And I will show the second part in a second. Could you just explain what this part of the map which is attached to your order, what this is about.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an integral part of the order to attack and the decision of the commander on the map, that is also approved by the corps commander in the upper left-hand corner and signed by me in the lower right-hand corner, and it depicts the order of the commander as specified in a textual form in the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And we see here on the first page the abbreviation in the middle: "Sa od ol m." Could you just explain what this abbreviation stands for?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Together with the El Mujahedin Detachment."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And then it says: "E 2 mnb." What does this stand for?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the 2nd Manoeuvre Battalion. Here I must say that this part, where it says "joined forces," my task within the Farz operation is a decisive defence of all lines within the area of responsibility of the 35th Division to engage part of my forces in the attack and to take over the lines captured during combat activities. So as soon as a feature is captured, my forces would advance to take possession of such positions and the El Mujahedin Detachment and the 2nd Manoeuvre Battalion form the composition of the 3rd Corps, and they were attached to the area of responsibility of the 35th Division. For this operation, I did not have an order for re-subordination of the El Mujahedin Detachment, or at least I cannot recall one.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. So if they were not detached to you, who was commanding the ordered El Mujahedin for this operation?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the corps commander's order, it was said that the forces -- the joint forces of the division will be strengthened by the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So who is commanding the El Mujahedin Detachment in this operation?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corps has laid down this mission, and later on when the operation started, we will see that the reporting line goes back to the corps commander, and he is carrying out this mission in my area of responsibility. So this is a moot point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just get clarification. Do I understand you, sir, to say that the El Mujahedin Detachment was re-subordinated to your division for each operation? It was not just re-subordinated and made part of your division. It had to be re-subordinated for every time you have to go for a -- for an operation? Is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. They were not part of the composition of the 35th Division. It was part of the composition of the 3rd Corps, but they were re-subordinated to me for certain combat operations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'd like to see that re-subordination order at some stage before the witness goes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I understood the witness to say that for this operation, Farz, you had not received such a re-subordination order. Could you just clarify for -- for Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order that I received on the 2nd of July for Proljece II Operation, where the commander said that the detachment were to be re-subordinated to the 35th Division and listed the missions for the detachment, that document that we saw yesterday, such an order was not received by me for the Farz operation, or at least I did not see one. It has not reached me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. If we look at the upper left-hand corner where it says "Sakib Mahmuljin," you mentioned earlier that you obtained a signature on such a map from him. If you look carefully --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the map had to be signed, as well as the order.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And interpreter's correction: It was the 2nd of June order, not 2nd of July. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So before the operation started, Mr. Mahmuljin had signed this map?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we can move to the last page of this document, the lower part of the map. If you look at the signature below there, who signed on the upper -- lower right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I signed this. Such a document must be signed by me and sent to the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to show you document PT2429 now. You see the document is from the 23rd of August, 1995, and it says: "Order for communications 4." In the upper right-hand corner, an "F" is mentioned. Could you explain what the "F" is standing for.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was supposed to state "F- 95." The "F" is short for the Farz operation or the Vozuca operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So am I right in saying that this order for communication relates to Operation Farz?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And could you explain what is the purpose of such an order for communication.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First I'd like to see the signature. This order is supposed to be prepared by the chief of staff, and he's supposed to sign it. But first I will have to see the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we look at the last page, please, on the B/C/S only. Yeah, I believe we have seen this document during our meetings and we saw that it was not signed. So I think this is unsigned, as you can see. Or can you direct me?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a chief of staff's document, and he's responsible for the establishment and functioning of communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We can actually go to the fifth page of the B/C/S, please. In the English, this page 10. Could you scroll down there. Yes, thank you. You see it's type signed and it says "Nesad Sabic." Who is Nesad Sabic?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nesad Sabic is the chief of staff of the division. And given this is a branch order, it has to be signed by the chief of communication as the highest officer in communications, and that was Captain Herceg in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What is the importance of communications during combat operation?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is one of an important elements. A key element is to have communications during carrying out of combat activities. And this document lists the command post, the forward command post, and the manner in which communications are to be maintained.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can the document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 462.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can we move to PT2438 now, the document from the 25th of August, 1995. And it says here: "Record of delivery of an order to attack with attachments." And we see here under number 1: "Order to attack." What order to attack is meant?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the basic combat document for the carrying out of combat operations. It regulates all the steps and procedures that the subordinates must adhere to during combat activities. The basic elements are the enemy, our forces, neighbouring forces, the decision, specific missions, and the conduct of all engaged in combat activities, including logistics and supplies, and, of course, command and communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Am I right in saying this is a kind of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we scroll down the English a little bit, please. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It's under number 1, "Order to attack," the witness has just explained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure. We wanted to see the order to attack. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So if we see -- on the English, move to page 2, under number 4 - if you can scroll down - I'm sorry, under number 8, "Communications plan." Was this the communication plan we just saw?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether this was specifically --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam -- Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, while the Prosecutor was asking questions about this other document, we were engaged in analysing the PT2429 document. This is the first time we see it. It was not included in a list. We received two lists. And that document, PT2429, was on neither list, so it is very difficult for us to follow what is being testified to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I can make an explanation. The witness has mentioned "communication" during the proofing sessions, and in the course of this session the document before was shown to the witness, and I have informed you via -- e-mail - I believe it was on Saturday - about the fact that this is a new document, because the witness wanted to refer to it. And I stated also the PT number. I even attached the English translation of the document, thereby informing you about my intention to show this document today.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please tell me at what time I was supposed to receive the e-mail message?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I will in the break make a printout of the e-mail and we can discuss it further.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I apologise for any inconvenience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Thank you, Mr. Neuner. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you look at the upper right-hand corner, there are the abbreviation "EL-M." Can you explain what is meant by this.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is short for "El Mujahedin." The title of the detachment is not contained here, and obviously the -- the operative concern wrote it this way. I don't recall the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What is meant by the upper right-hand corner here, "Komandi: EL-M"? Meaning, is this the addressee? Is this the sender? Is this...? Can you just explain?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We discussed documents yesterday, and we said that once an approval is received, the documents are sent to all the units participating in that given activity. I'm not sure whether this document is signed as well; however, a document similar to this one should have been handed over to the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I ask that the document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Does this mean that this -- this is a command to the El Mujahedin to carry out what is in the document, or what does it mean? What's the purpose -- what does -- what's the meaning of this "Komandi EL-M"? Is that an order to them to do something or what is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To have the documents listed further below delivered to them. The whole set of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 463.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And while the document is being admitted, we have just found the e-mail. It was sent on the 22nd of September in the afternoon at 2 hours, 19 minutes, for my learned colleagues -- in the afternoon at -- I am informing there about the PT number of the document and I'm attaching also the English translation of it. Thank you. I want to move to the next document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, your learned friend is on her feet. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my apologies for interrupting the proceedings. I do believe that the Prosecution ought to deliver documents in a timely fashion. From what I gather, the document was sent to us over the weekend, and I did not have occasion to look at the document, as I was busy preparing myself on the basis of others. As far as I know, the Prosecution has the duty to give us documents two days ahead. We received these two lists with all the documents there. Obviously the Prosecution sent this additional document over the weekend, and I did not have occasion to look through it. At any rate, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But, Madam Vidovic, if you say as far as you know, the Prosecution has the duty to give you documents two days ahead, today is the 25th and it was sent on the 22nd. That's three days ahead. Have they not complied with their duty? As you explained --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, they have. I apologise, Your Honours. I only stated that I failed to see the document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I ask that -- sorry. I'm a little bit confused. Because the document just shown now admitted? Yes, it was. I apologise. I want to move on to the next document, PT2438. Sorry, we just had it. 2527, PT2527.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is a document, we see, from the 6th of September, 1995, entitled "Deployment Rota for the Commanding Officers of the 35th Division." If we could go to the last page in B/C/S so that the witness can see the signature. Who signed?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we go back to the first page -- sorry -- yeah, the first page in B/C/S; in English, page 2. In the first paragraph here, an IKM of the 35th Division Babilon is mentioned. Could you explain where that IKM was.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is the deployment rota of commanding officers during combat involving several command posts: The forward command post of Babilon was 12 kilometre away from Zavidovici along the road leading to Vozuca, Hajdarovici [phoen], and the witness mentioned another locality. This is a large intersection of dirt roads. It is in the immediate vicinity of -- or rather, in the direction of the Paljenik feature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And can you explain -- it says, under number 1, the "commander." Who is meant by the "commander"?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there at the Babilon IKM, and the command -- or rather, the combat group that was there with me -- in other words, there was this combat group with all the additional services and branches there with me at IKM Babilon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you and others are manning the IKM Babilon. When were you manning the IKM Babilon? When did you begin to man it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was on the 8th or the 9th -- no, I believe it was the 9th of September, one day ahead of the start of Operation Vozuca. Previously, for several days the operations officers and others were preparing the IKM, trying to make it operational with the communications systems and everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: How long did you stay at that IKM following the 9th of September?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the first day of the operation, I was present at this IKM. On the second day of the operation, while it was ongoing, I frequently left the IKM in the direction of the area where our units were active. I would then go back there. It's hard to say whether it was one, two, or three days, because as the combat activities were moving northwards, I followed suit by setting up IKMs in that direction in order to be able to have a view of fighting and to be able to direct it. My position was - and this is something my subordinates knew and were aware of - as soon as combat activities started, they had to be deployed at one of the locations designated in order to continue with the combat activities and to be successful in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can the document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit 464.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Moving on to PT2536. The previous document was from the 6th of September, and now we see a document from the 7th of September, 1995. Who signed it?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And it says: "Supplement to order for attack of the 35th Division commander." I'm interested in the first line of the document, which states: "Pursuant to an assessment of the situation and an agreement with the commands of the El Mujahedin Detachment and the 3rd Manoeuvre Battalion for the execution of a task under the F-95 plan." The F-95 plan is the Farz plan, as we discussed; correct?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you explain who was entering into the agreement which is mentioned in the first line.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document tells us that the two neighbouring units, the 3rd Manoeuvre Battalion and the El Mujahedin Detachment, agreed on the best way to carry out combat activities. Since they were adjacent units, neighbouring units, they agreed upon it and I drafted this order, since the 3rd Manoeuvre Battalion belonged to my composition. The 3rd Manoeuvre Battalion went along the Krivaja River Canyon, which was in the direction of the Paljenik feature, and it was only logical for it to move that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what did the El Mujahedin Detachment do on the day of the operation? Which attack line was the El Mujahedin Detachment on?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Popov Osoje and Paljenik. Pod Palje [phoen] and Paljenik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can the document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 465.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to move to Exhibit 394, and I'm particular interested in entry number 6, which relates to the 9th of September; namely, at 20.40 hours. In English it's, I believe, page 6 -- excuse me, page 2. And in B/C/S, the second page. This is an operations -- operations diary of the 3rd Corps. And if you look at entry number 6 --

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen this document. This document is kept by the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you for this explanation.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the document is ...

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Please go ahead with your explanation.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document is a record of brief orders issued by the corps commander. Everything that goes on during combat activities which is of significance will be registered in the diary. This is a very important document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you look at entry number 6, it says: "The commander of the 35th Division informed the commander of the 3rd Corps that everything was going according to plan." Where -- first of all, do you recognise informing Mr. Mahmuljin at 8.15 in the evening on the 9th of September, 1995.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I set up my IKM ahead of combat activities, I had to inform the commander that I had set up an IKM, that I was there, and that we can have smooth future communications from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. So you were at IKM Babilon at this moment when you're informing him?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the last two questions were leading questions. In particular, the latter one. Can my learned friend from the Prosecution please refrain from putting leading questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We have explained with the previous document, which stated "IKM Babilion," and I was asking the witness where he was when he moved into IKM Babilon, and he said he moved into IKM Babilon on the 9th of September. And this entry here is from the 9th of September in the evening. So in a way I was leading - I agree with my learned colleague - on the other hand side, I picked up on what the witness had said earlier.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness stated that the IKM was located at Babilon and that he was there on that day. This, however, does not mean that he was stationary and unable to go elsewhere. The witness has just explained what his movements were and what the movements of the forces participating in the activities were. The witness said that he was at the IKM and that he moved along with the movement of the forces. That's why I believed the question was a leading one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I -- I hear what you say, Madam Vidovic. But if you look at the question before that one, he -- when he's being asked whether he remembered making a report to Mr. Mahmuljin at 8.15 on the 9th of September, he says: "When I set up my IKM ahead of combat activities, I had to inform the commander that I had set up my IKM." So, now, the IKM that he had just set up is the Babilon IKM. So the next question was: Was it -- is it Babilon where you were? I understand the formulation was leading, but the point had been -- had been established. Would you agree? Thank you very much, madam.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Where was Mr. Mahmuljin when you informed him in this remark number 6 --

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The IKM of the 3rd Corps was at Luke, 17 kilometres away from Zavidovici in the Kamenica area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. I want to move to the next entry. 45 minutes later, entry number 7 says: "The commander of the El Mujahid and Ajman had a meeting with the 3rd Corps commander at the 3rd Corps IKM-1." My question is: Where were you when that meeting just described here was taking place?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of the meeting. I don't know if it indeed took place. I was -- I was at the Babilon IKM. This is the first time I hear of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just get clarification. You've just told us that Mr. Mahmuljin was at the IKM of the 3rd Corps at Luke, 17 kilometres away from Zavidovici in the Kamenica area. Now, this IKM-1 that is on the entry - dash 1 - is it -- is it different from the IKM of the 3rd Corps? Is it another IKM or is it the same thing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please proceed, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. If we could please move to entry number 40. It's page 7 of the English translation and 6 of the B/C/S translation. Yes. It says here: "The 35th Division commander informed the 3rd Corps commander of the combat activities so far." Can you confirm?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I received information about what had transpired up to that point, at 9.49 I informed the -- the commander about what I had learned and about what had transpired in the activities so far. That's part of the regular reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What day are you informing him here?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was on the 10th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When did the operation start?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operation started on the morning of the 10th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you were reporting at 11 minutes to 10.00 when the operation has started to Mr. Mahmuljin. Could you tell me, who was in charge of Operation Farz?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corps commander was in charge of the Operation Farz.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Mahmuljin?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And why are you reporting back to him?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because he was in command of the entire operation. I only had a fraction of that mission, and I said at the outset what that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we look at entry number 55. In English, it's page 10. I think it's page 9 - yeah - in B/C/S. It the says here: "The 3rd Corps commander ordered the 35th Division commander that the 3rd Manbat is going along the road of the village Stog and further for mopping up." Can you confirm that you received that order?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. Can the Prosecutor ask the witness whether he issued the order, whether he informed. The Prosecutor consistently reads a portion of the text and then asks the witness whether he can confirm what was read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not sure what you mean by "ask the witness whether he issued the order, whether he informed." Informed who about what?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I meant, Your Honour, was that the Prosecutor has been reading parts of the text in -- for the witness instead of putting questions to him in relation to the contents of the diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I was asking whether he received the order. The entry says that the 3rd Corps commander ordered. I can rephrase the question and ask the witness, having seen --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The objection is you do the reading of the text in the entry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Instead of putting your question to the witness. That's the objection. Do you have any response to that one?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'll stop doing this for the future will just ask the witness, now I have read it out, I will just ask the witness whether he can comment upon the entry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you please comment upon the entry, Witness.

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall this period of time or this order. It's quite difficult for me to remember this now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall in general having received orders on the 10th of September from Mr. Mahmuljin?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We weren't much in touch on the 10th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When did you meet Mr. Mahmuljin, if at all, in this time period?

utterances.speaker: FADIL HASANAGIC [Resumed]
